nested_lists.name: owner_partner_shareholder_records
nested_lists.shape_reason: per-field wrapping (heavy) is affordable because owner counts are small (typically 1-5); each record needs name + ownership % + distribution/K-1 share, and the ownership % is what attributes income to the borrower. Mirrors the tax_return.schedule_c precedent

fields.name: owner_name
fields.why: attributes business income to the named owner

fields.name: ownership_percentage
fields.why: the ownership % that attributes income to the borrower (percent, no coercer, kept as string)

fields.name: distribution_or_k1_share
fields.why: the distribution / K-1 income share paid to the owner

rejected.name: party_names / party_addresses
rejected.reason: generic; superseded by typed business/owner fields

rejected.name: returns_allowances_and_cogs
rejected.reason: components of gross profit already captured; catch-all suffices

rejected.name: other_income, meals_and_nonrecurring_expenses, officer_or_owner_compensation
rejected.reason: candidate lists deferred — budget one list, zero rules; top-line add-backs captured as scalars

rejected.name: property_address, loan_number
rejected.reason: not on a business return face

rejected.name: issuer_name, issuer_address, issuer_phone, issuer_email_or_url, form_number, form_revision_date
rejected.reason: the return is self-identifying via return_form_type

rejected.name: document_title, document_status_or_version, signature_blocks, notary_block, paid_preparer_information (full object)
rejected.reason: execution/identity detail beyond the flattened fields kept

encoding_variations: The 'income' figure differs by form: 1065 line 'Ordinary business income', 1120S the same, 1120 'Taxable income' — return_form_type beside ordinary_or_taxable_income is the required disambiguator.
Fiscal-year filers state a period, not a calendar year; keep tax_period_start/_end rather than a single year so a fiscal year is unambiguous.
Add-backs appear on different lines/schedules (Form 8825, Schedule L, Form 4562); capture the top-line figure and let the snippet show its origin.

open_questions.q: Which nested list — owner_partner_shareholder_records (chosen, for income attribution) vs expense_line_items (for add-back detail) vs schedule_k_and_k1_summary. Only one fits the budget with zero rules.
open_questions.recommendation: keep owner records (attributes income to the borrower); revisit when a self-employed-income rule specifies exactly which schedule it reads

open_questions.q: List shape — per-field-wrapped chosen on the assumption of few owners. If a return can carry many shareholders, switch to flat-row to protect the 16,384-token ceiling.
open_questions.recommendation: flag item-count uncertainty; default to per-field-wrapped for typical 1-5 owners

open_questions.q: Add-backs as scalars vs list — depreciation/depletion/guaranteed-payments are kept as scalar top-line figures rather than in a list.
open_questions.recommendation: acceptable for zero rules; a cash-flow rule may later want the full expense list

notes: No rules read this document today, so there is no rule floor. This is the deepest of the eight but still Tier 3 — depth is capped at the figures a processor reads off the face of the return.

ein is the raw EIN (pre_masked false) and needs _PII_FIELDS registration; the snapshot masks it and adds a match-hash. The registry's employer_ein is stored masked — this raw-EIN catalog field is a distinct entry.
Owner/shareholder SSNs, if present on a K-1, must be promoted to a typed masked field within the nested record's redactor — never left to the catch-all.

Prompt hint (doc-level): this is a self-employed income source. Capture the income figure, the borrower's ownership %, and the standard add-backs verbatim; do NOT compute qualifying income or cash flow (a downstream calculation, not a fact).
Prompt hint (doc-level): report money as strings (e.g. '152340.00'); negative income keeps its sign. Ownership % lives in the owner records, tied to each owner's name.
Ambiguity: signature_date is tagged 'execution', which is not one of the five reason_class values — mapped to processor as best guess.
Ambiguity: paid_preparer_name is tagged 'source', which is not one of the five reason_class values — mapped to processor as best guess.
